FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Sixth Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standard, after the draft finalized by 
the Agricultural Machinery and Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture 
Division Council. 


This standard was first published in 1961 as specification for single-barrel stirrup-pump for public health use. 
With a view of widening the scope of the standard to cover the requirements for agricultural use as well, the first 
revision was published in 1965. Subsequently, the second, third and fourth revision of the standard were published 
in 1972, 1975 and 1982 respectively. A need was felt again to revise the standard in line with the revision of other 
sprayer standards. The fifth revision was done in the year 1996, whereby, materials of construction were modified 
and chemical composition of brass casting components as per relevant Indian Standard were given to ensure 
conformity. Also, the requirement of hydraulic agitator was made optional for the sprayer that is meant for 
agricultural use. 


In this revision, the following changes have been incorporated: 


a) Technical data has been elaborated and explained through respective figures and clauses; 

b) Performance test methods and test for components have been incorporated which were earlier covered in 
IS 10134 : 1994; 

Addition of further details as Annex C (hand operated cut-off device), Annex D (spray lance) and 
Annex D (hydraulic spray nozzle) has been made which were earlier covered in IS 3652 : 1995; and 
Necessary editorial changes have been made including updating of referred Indian standards and the 
schematic diagrams given in the standard.

This standard contains 10.2 which call for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. For the guidance of 
the purchaser, information to be supplied if quoted to the manufacturer is given in Annex B. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex F. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with. the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the results of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 1971 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


CROP PROTECTION EQUIPMENT — HAND-OPERATED 
STIRRUP-TYPE SPRAYER — SPECIFICATION 


( Sixth Revision ) 


1SCOPE 


1.1 This standard specifies material, performance, 
constructional and other requirements of hand- 
operated stirrup type sprayer (also called as 
Mechanical Sprayer) used for spraying plant 
protection substances (for example, pesticides). 


1.2 The maximum working pressure of this type of 
sprayers is 400 kPa (100 kPa = 1.0197 kgf/m? = 1 bar). 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this standard, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the edition indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreement based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent edition of these standards. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions in addition to those given in IS 8480 
shall apply (see Fig. 1 and 2). 


3.1 Cycle — One up and one down stroke. 


3.2 Gasket — A compressible insert placed between 
two surfaces to obtain a liquid or gas tight sealing. 


3.3 Guide — A component for guiding the 
movement of the piston rod. 


3.4 Handle — A component on the piston rod. 


3.5 Hose Connection — Device for connecting the 
delivery hose with the discharge outlet and the cut- 
off device. 


3.6 Piston — A component for creating pressure or 
suction and pressure. 


3.7 Piston Displacement — A volume displaced by 
piston during one stroke. 


3.8 Piston Rod — A rod or tube to help the 
movement of piston. 


3.9 Pump Cylinder — A component to guide the 
movement of piston. 


3.10 Spreader — A component for holding the 
piston in its shape and position. 


3.11 Stirrup-Pump — A pump, with footrest and 
stirrup, for producing spray. 


3.12 Stroke — The maximum travel of the piston 
rod in one direction when the handle moves from its 
lowest possible position to its highest possible 
position. 


3.13 Total Mass — The mass of complete sprayer 
with all its mountings but without any liquid and 
discharge line, that is, without delivery hose, cut-off 
device, lance and nozzle. 


3.14 Travel Limiting Device — A device for 
limiting the stroke. 


3.15 Valve Assembly — A device provided to 
check or to allow the flow of the fluid. 


3.16 Volumetric Efficiency — The quotient of the 
division of the actual volume of the spray fluid 
discharged in one stroke by the piston displacement, 
expressed as percent. 


3.17 Tank Nominal Volume — The volume 
indicated by the maximum filling level marked on 
the spray tank when placed on a level horizontal 
surface tank. 


3.18 Tank Capacity — The volume of tank when 
liquid is filled to its neck level, provided the tank is 
equipped with all its internal mountings. 


4MATERIAL 


4.1 The material of construction of various 
components of the sprayer shall be selected from 
col (3) of Table 1. The material other than brass 
casting should conform to the relevant 


IS 1971 : 2023 


Indian Standards, however brass casting 
components shall conform to the chemical 
composition as specified in IS 292 (grade to be 
declared by the manufacturer). 


4.2 The material for spray lance, nozzle, cut-off 
device and its components shall be as given in 
Table 1. 


4.3 All metallic parts coming in contact with the 
pesticide should preferably be of the same material 
to minimize bimetallic corrosion. 


4.4 The material for various parts shall be declared 
by the manufacturer in the manual (see 8.1).

6 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 
6.1 Discharge Rate 


When tested in accordance with the method given 
in 12.1, the pump shall be capable of discharging a 
minimum of 400 ml and 550 ml of water per minute 
for agricultural and public health application 
respectively.

6.2 Volumetric Efficiency 


When tested in accordance with the method given 
in 122, the volumetric efficiency shall not be less 
than 85 percent. 


6.3 Endurance 


The sprayer shall withstand the test prescribed 
in 12.3. 


7 CONSTRUCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
7.1 Height 


The overall height of the assembled pump from the 
bottom of foot rest to the top of the handle, handle 
being at its lowest position, shall be in the range of 
600 mm to 800 mm (see A in Fig. 1). 


7.2 Total Mass 


The mass of (see 3.13) of the sprayer shall not be 
more than 5 kg. 


7.3 Pump Cylinder 


The inner diameter of the pump cylinder shall not 
be more than 30 mm. The pump cylinder shall 
withstand test prescribed in 13.1. 


7.4 Piston 


The height of the straight portion of the piston shall 
be 13 mm minimum. In case, the piston is made out 
of synthetic rubber, it shall withstand the test 
prescribed in 13.2. 


7.4.1 Spreader 


If provided, it shall be able to hold the piston in its 
position without distortion against the wall of the 
pump cylinder. 


7.5 Piston Rod 


The piston rod shall not be less than 9.0 mm in 
diameter. 


IS 1971 : 2023 
7.5.1 Buffer 


A buffer device shall be provided on piston rod in 
order to prevent the direct impact of handle on pump 
body. 


7.5.2 Travel Limiting Device 


A Travel limiting device shall be provided on piston 
rod. The actual stroke length shall be declared by 
the manufacturer. 


7.5.3 The piston rod shall withstand the test 
prescribed in 13.3. 


7.6 Handle 


The handle shall be of “Р” or “Т” shape. If it is of 
*D' shape (see Fig. 1), it shall have an inside grip 
not less than 200 mm long with inside vertical 
clearance of not less than 75 mm. The grip shall be 
attached with handle support. If it is of ‘T?’ shape, 
the length of either side from the centre of the piston 
rod shall be not less than 100 mm. The diameter of 
the handle of both the types shall be not less than 
25 mm. 


7.7 Guide and Gland Packing 


A guide at the top of the pump cylinder shall be 
provided. The gland packing shall be enclosed with 
guide. 


7.8 Foot Valve 


A detachable foot valve consisting of suction valve 
and strainer shall be attached at the lower end of the 
pump cylinder. 


7.8.1. Strainer 


The strainer shall be of removable type. Any side or 
diameter of the apertures of the strainer shall not be 
more than 625 mm. 
NOTE — For measuring size of apertures, select 
10 consecutive apertures in the strainer and measure each 


side or diameter as case may be. Average the measured 
value and report. 


7.8.2 Hydraulic Agitator 


A hydraulic agitator-cum-relief valve shall be 


provided either equipped in the foot valve assembly 
or attached separately in case the sprayer is meant 
for public health. 


7.9 Stirrup and Foot Rest 


The stirrup shall be fitted with pump cylinder 
through a clamp. The pump cylinder and stirrup 
shall be in proper alignment to obtain the necessary 
balance while using the pump. 


7.9.1 A foot rest shall be attached at right angle to 
the stirrup. In case of foot rest of elliptical shape, the 
major and minor axis shall be minimum of 200 mm 
and 150 mm respectively when measured across 
outside to outside. 


7.9.2 The stirrup shall have a minimum length of 
300 mm when measured from bottom of foot rest to 
topmost portion of stirrup. A clearance of minimum 
80 mm (see B in Fig. 1) shall be maintained between 
the pump cylinder and the stirrup throughout their 
length. Provision shall be made to adjust the 
cylinder vertically with respect to the stirrup. 


7.10 Threaded Connections 


All metallic threaded connections of the sprayer and 
its components shall conform to IS 2643. The size 
designation and type of threads are as given in 
Table 2. For all the joining components with 
internal or external threaded connections, the 
engaged length of the threads shall not be less than 
6 mm. 

NOTE — The measurement of thread size shall be done 


by gauges and not by measuring absolute dimensions 
(see IS 10216). 


7.11 Delivery Spout 


A delivery spout having either straight or angular 
opening shall be provided. In case of angular 
opening, the angle between the axis of the opening 
and the piston a in Fig. 1 shall be minimum 45°. 
The spout shall be nipple type or threaded type. The 
length of the nipple shall be not less than 20 mm. 


7.12 Gaskets 


The gaskets of synthetic rubber and PVC whenever 
provided, shall withstand the test prescribed in 13.3.

IS 1971 : 2023 
7.13 Discharge Line 
7.13.1 Delivery Hose 


A delivery hose of suitable diameter and preferably 
5 min length shall be provided as agreed to between 
the purchaser and the supplier. The hose shall be 
connected with the delivery spout and the cut-off- 
device through hose connection (see Fig. 2). 


7.13.2 Hose Connection 


The hose connection for threaded and nipple type 
connections shall be of nut-nipple and clamp type, 
and clamp type respectively. The clamp shall be in 
the form of ferrule or clip. 


The hose and hose connection shall withstand the 
test prescribed in 13.4. 


7.13.3 Cut-off Device and Lance 


A cut-off device and lance shall be provided. These 
shall conform to the requirements as given Annex C 
and Annex D respectively. 


NOTE — In case of cut off device and spray lance of a type 
other than that specified in Annex C and Annex D is 
required by the purchaser, for the special purpose, its 
requirement shall be as agreed between purchaser and 
supplier. 


7.13.4 Nozzle 


Unless otherwise specified by the purchaser, the 
nozzle shall conform to the requirements of 
Annex E. 


8 OTHER REQUIREMENTS 
8.1 Manual 


The manual shall include technical specifications of 
the sprayer, material of construction of various 
components shown in the exploded view of the 
sprayer, instructions for operations апа 
maintenance, common faults and their remedies and 
safety precautions. Reference of IS 11429 shall also 
be given for the purpose of calibration of the 
sprayer. 


8.2 Spare Parts 


Spare parts, separately packed for each sprayer, 
according to the number required by the purchaser 
shall be provided. If no demand for spare parts has 
been made, a set of gaskets shall be provided with 
each sprayer. 


8.3 Optional Items 


At the option of the purchaser, the following item 
with the requirement indicated against that shall be 
provided in the sprayer. Any other optional items 
required by the purchaser shall be supplied; the 
requirement for the same shall be as agreed to 
between the purchaser and the supplier. 


8.3.1 Rubber Sheath 


The cylinder may be protected with a rubber sheath 
of minimum 3 mm thickness. 


8.4 Safety 


Each sprayer shall be provided with set of mask, 
hand gloves and safety goggles and apron. 


9 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 


9.1 The components of the sprayer shall have a 
smooth finish and shall be free from pits, burrs, 
sharp edges and other visual defects that may be 
detrimental for their use. 


9.2 The exposed mild steel parts shall have a 
protective coating to prevent surface deterioration. 
The steel used for hose ferrule/clip and buffer shall 
be plated with cadmium, zinc or nickel. Exposed 
brass parts may be given a suitable protective finish 
with clear transparent lacquer. 


10 MARKING AND PACKAGING 
10.1 Marking 
Each sprayer shall be marked with the following 


particulars: 


a) Manufacturer’s name or registered trade- 
mark; and 
b) Batch or serial number. 


10.2 Packing 


The sprayer shall be packed, as agreed to between 
the purchaser and the supplier, for safe handling in 
transit. 


10.3 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Асі, 2016 and the 


Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
products may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


11 SAMPLING FOR LOT ACCEPTANCE 


Unless otherwise agreed to between purchaser and 
the supplier, sampling of the sprayers for lot 
acceptance shall be done in accordance with 3 of 
IS 7201 (Part 1). 


12 PERFORMANCE TESTS 
12.1 Test for Discharge Rate 


12.1.1 The hydraulic agitator-cum-relief valve shall 
be taken out from its housing and the opening in the 
housing shall be sealed. 


12.1.2 The sprayer shall rigidly be mounted on the 
test bench (see Fig. 3) so that its suction side shall 
be submerged into a container filled with clean 
water. 


12.1.3 The piston rod or the handle of the sprayer 
shall be connected to an adjustable crank 
mechanism operated by a motor through a speed 
step-down drive so as to give a movement of 
16 + І cycles for one minute to the piston rod in such 
a manner as to maintain the proper alignment 
between the piston rod and pump cylinder. 


12.1.4 One end of a hose of 2 m length shall be 
connected to the discharge outlet of the sprayer and 
the other end to the inlet end of a straight rigid tube 
of 75 cm length and of 6 mm internal diameter. 


12.1.5 A pressure regulator shall be fitted at the 
outlet end of the rigid tube to adjust the pressure. 


12.1.6 An extension tube of suitable shape may be 
fitted at the outlet end of the pressure regulator for 
collecting the discharge of water in a container. 


12.1.7 A pressure gauge (see IS 3624), having full 
scale reading from 0 to not exceeding 2.5 times and 
not less than 1.5 times the normal working pressure 
of the sprayer, shall be fitted in the rigid tube at a 
distance of 15 cm from the inlet end of the pressure 
regulator on its up-stream side. 


12.1.8 The rigid tube with the pressure gauge and 
the pressure regulators shall be mounted on a 
separate test bench, other than the one with the 
driving unit, in order to eliminate vibration. 


12.1.9 The crank mechanism shall be adjusted so as 
to utilize the full stroke of the sprayer. 


IS 1971 : 2023 


12.1.10 The piston rod shall be operated at a 
constant speed of 16 + 1 cycles per minute. 


12.1.11 The pressure regulator shall be adjusted to 
develop a pressure of 300 kPa and 75 kPa within a 
fluctuation of + 20 percent when tested for 
agricultural and public health purposes respectively. 
Additional pressure chamber may be mounted to 
reduce the pressure fluctuations during test. 


12.1.12 The discharge of water in one minute shall 
be collected and measured. 


12.1.13 The above test shall be repeated four times 
and the average value of the measured discharge 
shall be calculated. 


12.2 Test for Volumetric Efficiency 


12.2.1 The discharge of water in one minute or 
10 successive strokes shall be collected and 
measured in accordance with 12.1 for particular 
sprayer. 


Repeat the test four times and calculate average 
value of the measured discharge. Calculate the 
volume of water in one cycle, that is, in one 
discharge stroke from the average measured 
discharge. 


12.2.2 Calculate the piston displacement by 
measuring the inner diameter of the pump cylinder 
and the actual length or one stroke. The inner 
diameter of the pump cylinder shall be measured 
below the bell mouth of the cylinder. 


12.2.3 The length of one stroke shall be measured 
by subjecting the pump to a pressure of 300 kPa 
within a fluctuation of + 20 percent. 


12.2.4 Divide the value obtained in 12.2.1 by the 
value obtained in 12.2.2 and express the result in 
percentage. 


12.2.5 The volumetric efficiency shall be recorded 
in the test report. 


12.3 Test for Endurance 


12.3.1 The sprayer or pump shall be operated in 
accordance with the method given in respective 
discharge rate test (see 12.1) for a minimum period 
of 48 h without measuring the liquid. The period 
should be covered minimum with continuous 
stretches of 6 h. 


IS 1971 : 2023 


ADJUSTABLE CRANK 
MECHANISM 


ELECTRIC MOTOR

12.3.2 The sprayer or pump shall not show any 
leakage or breakdown during the test. 


NOTES 


1 For routine and acceptance check, the sprayer or pump 
shall be run for a minimum period of 5 min instead of 
48 h. 


2 For hose and hose connection, lance and cut-off device, 
strength test may be conducted at one time. 


3 The piston and gasket test shall be conducted with a new 
set of pistons end gaskets provided with the sprayer. 


13 TESTS FOR COMPONENTS 


13.1 Test for Leakage and Deformation of 
Pressure Chamber, Pump Cylinder and 
Pressure Tank 


13.1.1 Pneumatic Test 


A hose shall be attached to the opening of the 
pressure chamber or pump cylinder or tank. In case 
there are a number of openings, other than the one 


to which the hose is attached, those openings shall 
be sealed. The pressure chamber or pump cylinder 
or tank shall then be pneumatically pressurized to a 
minimum of one and a half times the normal 
working pressure of the sprayer and the pressure 
shall be retained for a period of one minute. The 
component shall be disconnected, immersed in 
water and examined for any leakage and 
deformation. 


The pressure chamber or pump cylinder shall not 
show any leakage or deformation during the test. 


13.1.2 Hydraulic Test 


With the similar connection as that of 13.1.1, the 
pressure chamber or pump cylinder or tank shall be 
pressurized to a static hydraulic pressure of a 
minimum of two and a half times the normal 
working pressure of the sprayer and the pressure 
shall be retained for a period of one minute. The 
pressure chamber or pump cylinder or tank shall be 
examined for any leakage or deformation. 


The pressure chamber or pump cylinder or tank 
shall not show any leakage or deformation during 
the test. 


13.2 Test for Gasket and Piston 


13.2.1 All the gaskets in the sprayer shall be 
immersed in its test mixture of 60 percent kerosene, 
5 percent benzene, 20 percent toluene and 
15 percent xylene for a period of 72 h at a 
temperature of 27 °C to 33 °C and then dried in air 
at the same temperature range for 24 h. The gaskets 
shall then be fitted back in their original position. 


13.2.2 The sprayer connected with its discharge 
line shall be operated at its normal working 
conditions for one hour. 


13.2.3 The gaskets fitted at the points shall not 
show any leakage during the test. 


NOTE — Gasket test shall be conducted at the end of all 
the tests with new set of gaskets. 


13.3 Test for Handle, Piston Rod, Foot Rest and 
Stirrup 


This test shall be conducted in case of stir-up type 
sprayer as under: 


13.3.1 The discharge outlet of the sprayer shall be 


IS 1971 : 2023 


closed, that is, no discharge shall be allowed from 
the sprayer and the handle shall be operated to 
develop pressure in the sprayer until a pressure of 
minimum two and half times the normal working 
pressure is developed (in case it is not possible to 
develop minimum pressure of two and half times 
the normal working pressure by the operation of 
handle, the pressure shall be developed in the 
sprayer from any other source). 


13.3.2 These parts shall not break, deform or crack 
when the force is exerted at test pressure by moving 
the handle. 


13.4 Test for Hose and Hose Connection 


The inlet of the hose shall be connected to a 
hydraulic pump through hose connection. The other 
end of the hose shall be connected to the appropriate 
cut-off device. The outlet of the cut-off device shall 
be closed, that is, no discharge is allowed. A 
minimum hydrostatic pressure of 1.5 MPa, using 
water as a liquid, shall be developed in the host 
assembly and the pressure shall be retained for a 
period of 1 min. 


13.4.1 The hose and hose connection shall not 
show any leakage, crack or breakage during the 
test.

ANNEX C 
(Foreword and Clause 7.13.3) 
HAND-OPERATED CUT-OFF DEVICE 


C-1 TYPES 
The cut-off device shall be of the following types 
(see Fig. 4 and 5): 
a) Trigger type (Type A); and 
b) Knob type (Type B) 
C-2 DIMENSIONS 


C-2.1 The cross-sectional area of passage in valve 
body for liquid shall not be less than 12.0 mm?. 


C-2.2 The diameter of the valve stem shall be 
minimum 5 mm. 


C-2.3 The length of the operating trigger, in Type A 
cut-off device, from the pivot axis shall be 
minimum 100 mm. 


C-3 STRAINER 


C-3.1 The cut-off device may be provided with a 
strainer on its outlet side, the flow of the liquid 
through strainer shall be from outward to inward. 


C-3.2 The strainer area shall not be less than 
1 000 mm?. 


C-3.2.1 The average size of any sides or diameter of 
apertures of the strainer shall not be more than 
450 um. 


NOTE — For measuring the size of apertures, select 
10 consecutive apertures in the strainer and measure each 
side or diameter as the case may be. Average the measured 
value and report. 


IS 1971 : 2023

FIG. 5 KNOB TYPE (TYPE B) CUT-OFF DEVICE 


C-4 END-FITTINGS 


C-4.1 The inlet end-fitting of the cut-off device for 
connecting the delivery hose, shall be nipple type or 
thread type. The length of the nipple shall not be less 
than 20 mm. 


C-4.2 The outlet end-fitting of the cut-off device for 
connecting the lance shall be of thread type. 


C-5 GASKETS 


End fittings of thread type shall be provided with 
gaskets. If fitted to the external thread, it shall be 
recessed for at least one third of its thickness. Where 
fitted to internal thread, it shall at no time obstruct 
the passage of the liquid. 


C-6 OPERATING TRIGGER/KNOB 


C-6.1 The operating trigger in Type A cut-off 
device shall be attached with valve stem. A locking 
device shall be fitted which may be in the form of 
ring sliding over the trigger when the valve is in 
open position. 


C-6.2 When tested in accordance with the method 
given below, the maximum torque required for 
trigger actuation shall not be more than 3.5 Nm 
(35 kgf/cm). 


A suggestive arrangement for measuring the torque 
required to activate the cut-off device is shown in 
Fig. 6. The procedure for measurement is as given 
below: 


a) The cut-off device shall be mounted on a 
support rigidly; 


b) A U bolt or other arrangement of pre- 
known mass shall be hung for putting the 
weight at the rear most free end of the 
trigger; 


c) The distance (D) between the pivot point 
and the point of hanging or bolt or similar 
arrangement shall be measured; 


d) The weightof known mass shall be applied 
gradually till the point of application of 
trigger reaches from its highest position to 
the lowest possible position. Carefully 
observe the actions while reaching the 
lowest possible position. Calculate the 
total weight W by adding the mass of the 


OPERATING 
TRIGGER 


SPRAY LANCE 


IS 1971 : 2023 


weights and the mass of the bolt or 
arrangement on which the weights were 
added; 


e) The torque shall be calculated by 
multiplying D and W; and 

f) The test shall be repeated and the average 
value in Nm (kgf.cm), shall be reported. 


C-6.3 The operating knob in Type B cut-off device 
shall be suitably shaped for convenient handling. 


C-7 TESTS 


The cut-off device shall withstand the strength, 
leakage and reliability tests as given in C-7.1 and 
C-7.2. 


C-7.1 Strength Test of Cut Off Device 


C-7.1.1 The inlet of the cut-off device shall be 
attached with a delivery hole and shall be coupled 
to a hydraulic pump. 


C-7.1.2 The outlet of the cut-off device shall be 
closed, that is, no discharge shall be allowed from 
the device. 


C-7.1.3 A hydraulic pressure of minimum 750 kPa 
shall be applied at the inlet of the device. The 
pressure shall be maintained for a period of 5 min. 


C-7.1.4 During this test, the cut-off device shall not 
crack or burst. 


WEIGHT 
PLATFORM 


FIG. 6 ARRANGEMENT OF TRIGGER ACTUATION TEST 


IS 1971 : 2023 
C-7.2 Leakage and Reliability Test 
C-7.2.1 Test Apparatus 


The test apparatus shall be vibration free and shall 
be so arranged that the valve of cut-off device can 
be activated at a speed of not more than 15 cycle per 
minute. 


C-7.2.1.1 A typical test apparatus for trigger type 
cut-off device are given in Fig. 7 and Fig. 8. The 
dimensional and other details of cam follower and 
cam follower assembly except for cams given in 
Fig. 8 are for guidance purpose only. The cam | in 
Fig. 8 shall be used for operating the cut-off device. 
Cam 2, if provided, may be used to operate a timing 
switch for counting the number of cycles. 


C-7.2.1.2 A typical test apparatus for knob type cut- 
off device is given in Fig. 9. 


C-7.2.2 Test Liquid 


The test liquid shall consist of a 5 percent 
suspension of any commercially available water 
dispersible powder. The test liquid shall be changed 
after every 6 months of use. 


C-7.2.3 Test Method 


C-7.2.3.1 The cut-off device or spray gun shall be 
rigidly mounted on the appropriate test apparatus. 


C-7.2.3.2 A spray nozzle or an orifice plate 
designed to deliver liquid approximately 0.75 litre 
per minute at a pressure of 300 kPa + 30 kPa shall 
be attached at the outlet of the device. The nozzle or 
orifice may discharge the liquid directly or through 
appropriate piping into reservoir from which the 
liquid is recycled. 


C-7.2.3.3 The test liquid shall be applied to the inlet 
of the cut-off device or spray under a static pressure 
of 300 kPa + 30 kPa or 600 kPa + 60 kPa 
respectively. The cut-off device or spray gun shall 
be operated for 5 000 cycles at a speed of 
approximately 15 cycles per minute. 


C-7.2.3.4 After operating for 5 000 cycles, the test 
shall be repeated for 500 cycles at a pressure of 
600 kPa + 60 kPa for cut-off device and at 
1 200 kPa + 120 kPa for spray gun. 


C-7.2.3.5 The cut-off device or spray gun shall 
shall not drip or leak through the valve during the 
test. 


C-8 MARKING 
Each cut-off device shall be marked with the 


following particulars: 


a) Manufacturer Name or recognized trade- 
mark; and 
b) Batch or code number.

ANNEX D 
(Foreword and Clause 7.13.3) 
SPRAY LANCE 


D-1 TYPES 


The lance shall be of following types (see Fig. 10): 
a) Straight type (Type A); and 
b) Gooseneck type (Type B): 
1) Single piece (Type Bı) 
2) Two piece (Type B»). 


D-2 MATERIALS 


Brass or stainless steel or plastic tube shall be used. 
The material for end-fittings shall be the same as 
that of the tube. 


D-3 DIMENSIONS 


D-3.1 Minimum thickness of the wall of the tube 
forming the lance shall be as given below: 
a) Brass tube — 0.60 mm; and 
b) Plastic tube — 3.0 mm. 


D-3.2 Internal diameter of the tube shall not be less 
than 6 mm. 


D-3.3 When measured vertically from sealing face 
to sealing face, as shown in Fig. 10 the nominal 
length of the lance shall be in between 500 mm and 
900 mm x 2.5 percent. 


D-3.4 At least three-quarter length of Type B lance 
shall be straight and then provide a bent to the 
remaining length, a radius of not less than 35 mm at 
an angle of 45? to 60? (see Fig. 10). 


D-4 OTHER REQUIREMENTS 


D-4.1 The lance shall be of a seamless construction. 


The both end-fittings shall be attached to the lance 
tube. 


D-4.2 The sealing face of the end-fittings shall be 
flat. In case of straight lance, the end-fitting on the 
cut-off device side shall have hexagonal or flattened 
faces; knurled faces or wing-nuts of adequate shape 
and size may also be provided. 


D-4.3 The lance shall withstand the test given 
in D-4.3.1. 


D-4.3.1 The inlet of the spray lance shall be attached 
to a hydraulic pump directly or through a delivery 
hose. The outlet of the lance shall be closed, that is, 
no discharge shall be allowed from the lance. A 
hydraulic pressure of 1 MPa or two-and-half times 
of the normal working pressure of the sprayer (for 
which the lance is meant), whichever is more, shall 
be applied to the lance up to a period of 5 min. 
During this test, the lance shall not leak, crack or 
burst. 


NOTE — In case of the information about the sprayer for 
which the lance is not known, the pressure of 1 MPa shall 
be applied. 


D-5 MARKING 


The lance shall be marked with the following 
particulars: 


a) Manufacturer's name or recognized trade- 
mark; and 
b) Nominal length. 


45* TO 60* 


45° TO 60° 


TYPE Bi

HOLLOW CONE 


FIG. 15 CONE OR SWIRL NOZZLE 


E-1.2 On the basis of the method of attachment, the 
nozzles shall be of the following types: 


a) Fixed type; and 
b) Swivel type. 


E-2 DESCRIPTION 


E-2.1 The nozzle may consist of various 
components as shown in their respective figures. 


E-2.1.1 A tangential velocity in the liquid emerging 
from cone nozzle orifice could be obtained either by 
passing it through a tangential or a helical slot in a 
swirl core or by sending it tangentially in the swirl 
chamber. Liquid is discharged from the orifice as a 
hollow cone of spray drops (see Fig. 15). Some 
nozzles of this type are adjustable producing any 
spray patterns from straight jet to wide angled 
hollow cone. The degree of atomization is governed 
by the relative sizes or swirl core and nozzle orifice. 


E-2.1.2 Fan nozzles produce a spray pattern in the 
form of the flat sheet. Generally, the nozzle tip has 
a narrow hole, that is especially shaped to curve 
inward towards its axis thus narrowing in 
immediately behind the orifice. The hole in nozzle 
is either rectangular or more commonly ventricular 
in shape. The size of the orifice governs the 
discharge rate at any given pressure. 


E-2.1.3 In case of an adjustable nozzle the liquid is 
discharged from the nozzle orifice in the form of 
cone spray or jet spray of any pattern upon the axial 
adjustment of the spindle or body. The swirl core 


may be integral part of the tip or separately attached. 
E-3 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 
E-3.1 Rate of Discharge 


E-3.1.1 The discharge rate of the nozzle shall be 
declared by manufacturer. In case of an adjustable 
nozzle, the declared value shall be for extreme 
adjustment for cone and jet spray patterns at a 
pressure of 300 kPa. 


E-3.1.2 When tested in accordance with E-7, the 
nozzle shall provide a rate of discharge as given in 
Table 3. The rate of discharge shall be within 
+ 5 percent for fixed type and + 10 percent for 
adjustable type nozzles of the declared value. 


E-3.2 Spray Angle 


The spray angle of the nozzle shall be declared by 
the manufacturer. The angle when tested in 
accordance with the method given in E-9 shall not 
differ by + 3° for fixed type and + 5° for adjustable 
type nozzles from the declared value. 


E-3.3 Endurance Test 


The hydraulic spray nozzle when tested in 
accordance with E-8 and E-9 at a pressure of 
300 kPa + 30 kPa after operating for 48 h duration 
with continuous stretches of 6 h, variation in 
discharge rate and spray angle from initial values 
should not be more than 5 percent and 
3° respectively.

E-5 DESIGNATION 


E-5.1 The cone and fan nozzle shall be designated 
by its identification mark [A for agricultural use and 
B for public health use (see Note in Table 3)], spray 
angle and discharge rate. An adjustable nozzle shall 
be designated by identification mark AN - C - J for 
cone and jet spray pattern and discharge rate at a 
controlled pressure of 300 kPa. 


Examples: 


A nozzle for agricultural use giving 90? spray 
angle with discharge rate of 300 ml/min shall 
be designated as: A 90300. 


A nozzle for public health use living 80? spray 
angle with discharge rate of 900 ml/min shall 
be designated as: B 80900. 


An adjustable nozzle capable of giving 60? spray 
angle with discharge rate of 600 ml/min during 
extreme adjustment of cone spray and discharge 
rate of 1800 ml/min during jet spray at a controlled 
pressure of 300 kPa shall be designated as: 
AN -C 60 600 -J 1800. 


E-6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 


E-6.1 The components of the spray nozzle shall be 
free from burrs and other defects; this applies 
particularly to the internal surfaces and specially to 
the orifice. 


E-6.2 The mating faces of the cap, tip and nozzle 
body or boss shall be finished flat so as to seal on 
the end face of the nozzle body or boss; a gasket 
may be used, if necessary. 


E-6.3 The screw threads shall be well formed and 
the crests of the threads shall be free from burrs or 
any other defects which may prevent free 
engagement. 


E-7 METHOD OF TEST FOR DISCHARGE 
RATE 


E-7.1 The nozzle under test, shall be connected to a 
supply of clean water or spray materials which are 
equal in density, surface tension and viscosity of 
water. The water or spray material shall be under a 
controlled pressure of 75 kPa or 300 kPa or 
600 kPa (as the case may be) with the pressure 
gauge (see IS 3624). The pressure gauge shall be 
positioned immediately before the nozzle and shall 
have full scale reading of pressure from 0 to not 
exceeding 2.5 times, not less than 1 time, that is to 
be read. The fluctuation of the pressure during the 


21 


IS 1971 : 2023 


test shall be not more than 10 percent from 
the controlled pressure. 


E-7.2 Turn on the supply and adjust the pressure and 
direct the spray for a period timed by stopwatch, 
into receiving vessel so designed as to collect whole 
of the spray from the nozzle. The period shall not be 
less than 60 s or not less than the time required to 
discharge 500 ml, whichever is higher. 


E-7.3 Direct the spray away from the vessel and turn 
off the supply. Measure the volume of the water or 
the spray material collected and calculate the 
discharge rate per minute. 


E-7.4 Repeat the above test for at least four times 
and obtain average rate of discharge per minute. 


E-8 METHOD OF TEST FOR 
DISTRIBUTION 


SPRAY 


E-8.1 Apparatus 
E-8.1.1 Patternator 


The patternator (see Fig. 17) normally consist of 
16 channels each 25 mm + 0.5 mm wide and of any 
convenient length provided that it encompasses the 
area of the spray. The number of channels may be 
increased or decreased so that the whole of the spray 
falls within the patternator. The channels guide the 
liquid directly to the measuring tube with maximum 
bore diameter of 24 mm. The measuring tube shall 
be long enough to hold at least of 200 ml test liquid. 
The depth of channels shall be at least 50 mm and 
shall have provision to avoid rebound of the spray 
droplets. The top edge of the trough dividers shall 
be round (tapered to 2.0 mm + 0.5 mm on the top 
edge) and straight in the horizontal plane, so that no 
point along with the edge lies more than 1 mm from 
the straight line joining the corresponding point at 
each end. The top edges of the dividers shall be 
positioned so that when a straight edge is laid across 
the full width of the front and back of the troughs no 
edge lies more than 1 mm below this. Each divider 
shall be straight in the vertical plane to within 
+0.5 mm. 


NOTE — The surface of patternator should be such that the 
droplets should not stick on it. 


E-8.1.2 A compressed air supply or small pump 
giving a steady output, with a liquid supply line 
from the reservoir of capacity two litres or more. 


E- 8.1.3 A constant pressure regulator and a 
pressure gauge should be installed as close to the 
nozzle as possible. 


IS 1971 : 2023 


E-8.1.4 Establish a suitable means of holding the 
nozzle at the appropriate height with the required 
facilities for adjustments. 


E-8.1.5 A test tube rack so made that the collecting 
tube can be inserted in the flow when constant flow 
has been achieved, and retracted after a 
predetermined period. 


E-8.2 Method 


E-8.2.1 Carry out the test directing spray, at 
standard rate of discharge and standard pressure, 
from the nozzle on the patternator protected by 
screens from draughts. 


E-8.2.2 In the case of fan spray nozzles, mount the 


nozzle so that the axis of spray sheet is right angle 
to the upper surface of the trough divisions on the 
patternator and the nozzle tip at a height of 545 mm 
above the trough division. In case of cone nozzle, 
mount the nozzles so that axis of its spray cone is at 
right angles to the upper surface of the trough 
division on the patternator and the nozzle tip at a 
height of 545 mm above trough divisions. 


E-8.2.3 Test the cone spray nozzle in three different 
positions of nozzles, namely, 90°, 180° and 270° 
(see Fig. 18). 


E-8.2.4 The total amount of liquid sprayed for each 
individual test shall be about one litre.

E-10 METHOD OF TEST FOR VARIATION 
IN DISCHARGE AND DISTRIBUTION DUE 
TO ABRASION AND CORROSION 


This test does not prejudge the life of a nozzle in the 
actual conditions of use, but is used to compare the 
resistance of wear of the nozzle and result of 
deterioration in the distribution. 


E-10.1 Test Liquid 


E-10.1.1 Clean water with the addition of 20 g/l of 
abrasive or corrosive material shall be used as a test 
liquid. The abrasive material may be a synthetic 
silica powder of following chemical and physical 
properties: 


SI No. Property Requirement 
(1) (2) (3) 
i) Bulk density 160 kg/m? 
ii) Specific gravity 1.95 
iii) Average particle size 0.002 2 um 
iv) Colour White 
v) Refractive index 135 to 165 
vi) Surface area 140 to 160 mg 


IS 1971 : 2023 


51 No. Property Requirement 
(1) (2) 3) 
vii) pH (5 percent water suspension) 7.3 
уш) Loss at 105 °C 5 percent 
ix) Loss at 1 200 °C 10 percent 
X) SO» content 87 percent 
xi) CaO content 0.5 percent 
xii) Fe203 content 0.2 percent 
xiii) Al,O3 content 0.6 percent 
Xiv) NaCl content 1.0 percent 


E-10.1.2 Ensure that the abrasive material is always 
well dispersed throughout the liquid. It may be done 
by means of controlled escape of compressed air 
with such a pressure so that after 5 min of operation, 
no deposit of abrasive material is left at bottom of 
tank. 


E-10.1.3 Ensure (if needed) by preliminary tests 
that the liquid retains its effectiveness in relation to 
the material of nozzle throughout the duration of 
the test defined in E-10.2. If it does not, replace the 
abrasive liquid as often as necessary. 


NOTE — It is possible to proceed using identical metering 
orifices from the same batch made from a suitable material 
in relation to nozzle being tested, measuring the increase in 
discharge rate after passing through a given volume of the 
test liquid at a specified pressure. 


E-10.1.4 The temperature of the test liquid as all be 
20 °C + 3 °C throughout the test. 


E-10.2 Method 


E-10.2.4 Measure the discharge rate at the 
beginning of the test at a controlled pressure (the 
fluctuation shall not be more than + 10 percent) and 
then every hour or at a regular interval chosen 
according to the speed of wear out of nozzle or at 
discharge of 4 litre intervals. It shall be continued 


25 


until the nozzle is abraded to the point where the 
flow increases beyond the allowable limit of 
6 percent. 


E-10.2.2 Carry out the spray distribution test 
(see E-8) at the beginning and at the end of the test 
for about 10 percent, 15 percent and 20 percent of 
increase in discharge rate if these values are 
reached. 


E-10.3. Result 


E-10.3.1 State in the test report, the increase in 
discharge rate thus obtained, expressed as a 
percentage of the initial discharge rate and as 
function of test period. 


E-10.3.2 Also give spray distribution observed at 
the various degree of wear indicated in E-10.2.2. 


E-11 MARKING 


Each nozzle shall be marked with the following 
particulars: 


a) Manufacturer's 
trade-mark; and 

b) Nozzle designation (see E-5); and 

c) Batch or serial number and date. 


name or recognized 


IS 1971 : 2023

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: FAD 11 (17071).
